title: Grateful Dead Live at The Ark on 1969-04-23
lineage: MSR > Cassette > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a stellar ’69 show highlighted by a soaring “He Was A Friend Of Mine”, an explosive Alligator/Eleven sequence and a memorable Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The recording offers a clear vintage soundboard source with only occasional splice or tape‑flip quirks, making it very listenable for a late‑early ’69 performance.  Musically the night shines on “He Was A Friend Of Mine”, the Alligator → The Eleven flow, Dark Star and the St. Stephen→It’s A Sin sandwich, while Jerry’s guitar work (sweet tone, slide wizardry) and Mickey’s frantic drumming draw consistent praise.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.5/5 across 16 detailed reviews; both the musical performance and recording quality are described as strong with only minor technical hiccups.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear vintage soundboard with good balance; a few tape‑flips/splices (St. Stephen→It’s A Sin, The Eleven) and occasional cuts are noted but do not detract significantly.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
St. Stephen > It's A Sin > St. Stephen
poor_songs: Alligator (a little sloppy according to one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows superbly with tight segues (Alligator → The Eleven, Morning Dew → AWBYG). Minor tape‑flip edits interrupt the flow slightly but overall the show feels cohesive and energetic.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for sweet tone on “He Was A Friend Of Mine”, slide brilliance on “Hard To Handle”, extra bursts of adrenaline in “We Bid You Goodnight”, and a subtle quote of “There Is A Mountain” during the Alligator jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: TC’s organ line bridges St. Stephen to It’s A Sin; glockenspiel noted during the transition, showing keyboard creativity.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s drumming described as “for dear life” in Caution and throughout the high‑energy sequences.
